title.narrative: Acute support to IDPs in Haiti

description.narrative:
The current crisis in Haiti, particularly in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area, is characterized by widespread insecurity, displacement, and growing humanitarian needs driven by escalating gang violence and political instability. With the escalation of violence in recent months, gangs have gained significant control over key neighbourhoods in Port-au-Prince, severely disrupting public order and limiting access to essential services such as healthcare, education, food and water. Violent clashes between rival gangs and law enforcement, along with frequent kidnappings, extortion, and roadblocks, have created a climate of fear, forcing thousands of people to flee their homes and seek safety in makeshift camps or overcrowded shelters, often set up in schools, and government buildings.
In addition to the violence, chronic poverty and limited state governance exacerbate the crisis. Many displaced people now live in unsafe, unhygienic conditions, lacking adequate food, clean water, sanitation, and medical care. The disruption of economic activities due to blockades and insecurity has further harmed livelihoods, leaving vulnerable populations without reliable sources of income. Women and children, who represent a large portion of the displaced, face heightened risks of exploitation, malnutrition, and inadequate healthcare, making them especially vulnerable to the ongoing crisis.
Humanitarian access remains challenging, with aid organizations facing restricted movement due to the threat of gang attacks. Despite these obstacles, addressing urgent needs through cash assistance, WASH services, and community support is critical to providing relief and stability to those affected within Port-au-Prince’s metropolitan area.

The direct beneficiaries of this intervention are 400 IDP households residing in two specific sites in Port-au-Prince, Lycée Marie Jeanne and Faculté Linguistique Appliquée. The selection and targeting process will focus on identifying the most vulnerable households, prioritizing those:
The selection process will prioritize households:
Without Shelter or Resources: Families lacking stable shelter or essential supplies.
Newly Displaced: Households affected by the recent escalation of violence.
Verified through Community Engagement: In collaboration with Haiti Survie, ensuring transparency and reaching those in most critical need.
Needs-Based Assessment: A needs assessment, conducted by Haiti Survie, will identify the most urgent requirements of IDPs. IDPs who lack shelter and food security will be the primary focus.
Coordination with Local Authorities and Clusters: Christian Aid and Haiti Survie will coordinate with local government bodies, the Cash Working Group (CWG), and WASH and Food Security Clusters to verify beneficiary lists and avoid duplications

The project aims to alleviate the humanitarian crisis faced by IDPs in Port-au-Prince, particularly at Lycée Marie Jeanne and Faculté Linguistique Appliquée. Its primary objective is to improve IDP households' living conditions and food security, ease overcrowding in educational institutions, and ultimately facilitate a return to normal school operations. By addressing urgent food and hygiene needs, the project supports IDP well-being and helps stabilize educational infrastructure.

title.narrative: CSH-R1: Number of people benefitting from unconditional and unrestricted cash transfers

description.narrative: Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments.

title.narrative: ACC-R1: Number of crisis-affected people who are also involved in the design, implementation, monitoring and/or evaluation of the programme

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. Participation does not take place when activities are carried out in exchange for a salary of 'in-kind' payment unless the affected people are involved in decision-making processes and have an impact on decisions that affect them. Please describe in the activity description what this involvement specifically entails and in which phase of the program conflict-affected people are involved.

title.narrative: WSH-R6: Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities. Could be training, campaigns, radio broadcasts, flyers etc. Excludes the distribution of Hygiene/dignity kits that should be covered under WHS-I1.
